organizations.name: Union Government of Myanmar
organizations.description: Executive body of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar. Current cabinet: second Min Aung Hlaing cabinet, formed 2026-04-10 after the 2025-26 general election (34-member government, 31 Union ministries). President Min Aung Hlaing elected by the 3rd Pyidaungsu Hluttaw on 2026-04-03.

key_people.title: President / Head of State and Government
key_people.name: Min Aung Hlaing

organizations.name: State Administration Council
organizations.description: Military governing council formed after the 2021-02-01 coup d'etat and the governing authority of Myanmar 2021-2025. Following the 2025-26 general election and the 2025-07 transition (Nyo Saw cabinet, later presidency of Min Aung Hlaing from 2026-04-10), its current institutional role is subject to change; verify against 2026 sources.

organizations.name: National Defence and Security Council
organizations.description: Top national security council of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar under the 2008 Constitution, chaired by the head of state. Reactivated by the military leadership after the 2021 coup; a central body in post-2025 power arrangements. Wikidata also hosts item Q137773946 as a disambiguation page.

organizations.name: Pyidaungsu Hluttaw
organizations.description: Bicameral Assembly of the Union (Pyithu Hluttaw + Amyotha Hluttaw). The 3rd Pyidaungsu Hluttaw seated after the 2025-26 general election elected Min Aung Hlaing president on 2026-04-03 and confirmed 31 Union ministries.

organizations.name: Office of the President of Myanmar
organizations.description: Union-level office supporting the President of Myanmar. Per the 2025-26 transition, the President is Min Aung Hlaing.

organizations.name: Supreme Court of the Union
organizations.description: Highest judicial forum and final court of appeal of Myanmar, an independent judicial entity alongside the legislative and executive branches. Mandated 7-11 judges including the Chief Justice.

organizations.name: Constitutional Tribunal of the Union
organizations.description: Constitutional Tribunal of Myanmar, interprets the 2008 Constitution and reviews laws for constitutionality.

organizations.name: Union Election Commission
organizations.description: Electoral commission of Myanmar. Under post-coup composition it administered the 2025-26 general election held in three phases (2025-12-28, 2026-01-11, 2026-01-25) and published results in which the USDP won over 72% of seats. Dissolved 40 parties (incl. NLD and SNLD) in March 2023 under the new Political Parties Registration Law.

organizations.name: Union Civil Service Board
organizations.description: Civil service commission of Myanmar responsible for civil service appointments and administration.

organizations.name: Office of the Attorney General
organizations.description: Union-level legal advisory and prosecution office of the Government of Myanmar (Union Attorney General's Office).

organizations.name: Myanmar National Human Rights Commission
organizations.description: National human rights institution of Myanmar.

organizations.name: Yangon City Development Committee

organizations.name: Tatmadaw (Myanmar Armed Forces)
organizations.description: Combined military forces of Myanmar (army, navy, air force). Institutional backbone of the post-2021 regime; Commander-in-Chief Senior General Min Aung Hlaing led the 2021 coup and became President in April 2026 after the 2025-26 election. Also known as Sit-Tat.

organizations.name: Myanmar Army
organizations.description: Ground forces branch of the Myanmar Armed Forces; largest branch and core of the Tatmadaw.

organizations.name: Myanmar Navy
organizations.description: Naval warfare branch of the Myanmar Armed Forces.

organizations.name: Myanmar Air Force
organizations.description: Aerial warfare branch of the Myanmar Armed Forces.

organizations.name: Myanmar Directorate of Defence Industries
organizations.description: Military industry directorate of Myanmar (KaPaSa), produces small arms and ammunition for the Tatmadaw.

organizations.name: Myanma Economic Holdings Limited
aliases: Union of Myanmar Economic Holdings Limited
organizations.description: UMEHL/MEHL, established February 1990 under the Special Companies Act as the economic arm of the Burmese military with initial capital of US$1.6 billion. Designated by OFAC on 2021-03-25 as a military holding company. Share dividends fund the military.

organizations.name: Myanmar Economic Corporation
organizations.description: MEC, one of the two major conglomerates/holding companies operated by the Burmese military (the other being MEHL); businesses include mining, manufacturing, telecommunications and banking. Designated by OFAC on 2021-03-25.

organizations.name: Defence Services Academy
organizations.description: Premier military academy of Myanmar (Batain, near Pyin Oo Lwin), trains officer cadets of the Tatmadaw.

organizations.name: Defence Services Medical Research Centre
organizations.description: Military medical research centre of the Myanmar Defence Services (Wikidata item created 2025; limited independent data).

organizations.name: Asia World Group
organizations.description: One of Myanmar's largest conglomerates (infrastructure, construction, ports, logistics).

organizations.name: Htoo Group of Companies
organizations.description: Major Burmese holding company founded by Tay Za; interests span aviation, construction, trading and tourism.

organizations.name: Max Myanmar Group
organizations.description: Major Burmese holding/construction conglomerate (Max Myanmar Holding).

organizations.name: Dagon International
organizations.description: Burmese conglomerate (timber, construction, food and agriculture).

organizations.name: Zaykabar Company
organizations.description: Construction-focused Burmese company (Zaw Zaw).

organizations.name: Yuzana Company
organizations.description: Burmese company (agribusiness, sugar, construction, real estate; Yuzana Plaza/Yuzana Garden City).

organizations.name: Shwe Taung Group
organizations.description: Myanmar business conglomerate (construction materials, real estate, retail: Junction malls). Ranked among the largest Myanmar companies by revenue (~US$1.9B, ZoomInfo Sep 2026).

organizations.name: IGE Group of Companies
organizations.description: International Group of Entrepreneurs (IGE), one of Myanmar's largest conglomerates with 13 subsidiaries; second-largest timber trader; established 1994.

organizations.name: City Mart Holdings
organizations.description: Leading retailer in Myanmar (City Mart, City Express, Ocean Supercenter chains).

organizations.name: Myint & Associates
organizations.description: Petroleum industry services company (oil and gas upstream services).

organizations.name: First Myanmar Investment
organizations.description: FMI Public Co., Ltd, founded 1992 as one of Myanmar's first public companies; subsidiary of Serge Pun & Associates; first company listed on the Yangon Stock Exchange (2016-03-25, code 00001). Portfolio includes Yoma Bank, Pun Hlaing Hospitals, Yoma Land and Memories Group.

organizations.name: ATOM Myanmar
organizations.description: Telecommunications operator of Myanmar; successor of Telenor Myanmar (rebranded ATOM after M1 Group acquired Telenor's Myanmar operations in 2022).

organizations.name: U9 Myanmar
organizations.description: Telecommunications company in Myanmar; formerly Ooredoo Myanmar (rebranded U9 after Ooredoo's exit).

organizations.name: Gamone Pwint
organizations.description: Myanmar retail company (supermarket chain).

organizations.name: Sein Gay Har
organizations.description: Myanmar retail company (supermarket chain).

organizations.name: Myanma Oil and Gas Enterprise
organizations.description: MOGE, the state-owned oil and gas enterprise of Myanmar under the energy portfolio; holds production sharing contracts with international oil and gas companies. History: nationalized oil industry 1963; current name adopted 1989. Described by Justice For Myanmar as Myanmar's most lucrative military-linked business after the 2021 coup.

organizations.name: Myanmar Posts and Telecommunications
organizations.description: MPT, state-owned enterprise operating Myanmar's postal system and a mobile network (joint operation with KDDI and Sumitomo Corporation).

relationships.target_name: Ministry of Transport and Communications (per Wikipedia; portfolio split in 2026 cabinet)

organizations.name: Myanma Timber Enterprise
organizations.description: State-owned timber enterprise of Myanmar (wood industry). Wikidata contains two items (Q19718582 and Q30266911) that may need reconciliation.

organizations.name: Myanma Gems Enterprise

organizations.name: Myanma Port Authority
organizations.description: Government agency/port authority of Myanmar managing major ports (Yangon, Thilawa).

organizations.name: Myanmar National Airlines

organizations.name: Myanma Railways
organizations.description: State-owned railway company of Myanmar (formerly Burma Railways), operates the national rail network; no dedicated Wikidata item confirmed (article 'Rail transport in Myanmar' Q750901 covers the network).

organizations.name: Myanma Insurance
organizations.description: The only state-owned insurance company of Myanmar, transacting life and non-life insurance; historically under the Ministry of Planning and Finance (portfolio now Finance and Revenue). No Wikipedia/Wikidata article confirmed.

organizations.name: University of Yangon

organizations.name: National League for Democracy
organizations.description: NLD, pro-democracy party of Aung San Suu Kyi; won 1990, 2015 and 2020 elections; governed 2016-2021. DISSOLVED by the junta-controlled Union Election Commission on 2023-03-28 (among 40 parties) for failing to register under the new Political Parties Registration Law; the NLD rejects the dissolution and continues activities from outside the official system. Caution: Wikidata/Wikipedia may not fully reflect dissolution status.
